content:
When the operator asks for a comprehensive review ("every check on every sheep", "run an analysis on every X", "document the results"), they want MANUAL per-item judgment, not script-generated check-list output.

Direct quote (operator, 2026-04-26): "YOU do the work, ANIMAL BY ANIMAL. Careful, not clever. Clever is scripts. careful is you."

ANTI-PATTERN (caught in this session): writing a Python script that emits uniform per-record bullet points (PASS/FAIL/INFO). Even when every bullet is factually correct, the output reads as machine-generated and the operator rejects it on sight ("thats not what i asked for", "nah nah nah").

CORRECT PATTERN: read each record in full, then write each finding by hand as prose. Label what you actually saw vs. what's inferred. Each subject gets its own section with judgment calls a reader can argue with.

Scripts are fine for data extraction, dumps, and validation. They are NOT fine as the deliverable for review work.

Resolved in manateecreeksheep@08e7b6e (manual docs/pen_3_analysis_2026-04-26.md, 449 lines by hand).
